name: Droperidol
metabolism: Droperidol is extensively broken down in the liver, undergoing oxidation, dealkylation, demethylation and hydroxylation by cytochrome P450 isoenzymes 1A2 and 3A4, and to a lesser extent by 2C19. The metabolites are devoid of neuroleptic activity. Elimination occurs mainly through metabolism; 75% is excreted via the kidneys, only 1% of the active substance is excreted unchanged in urine and 11% in faeces. Plasma the body clears it at 0.8 (0.4-1.8) l/min and the time in the body is 134 +/- 13 min. Plasma concentrations fall rapidly during the first 15 minutes after being given into a vein; this is a metabolism-independent redistribution, and plasma protein binding is 85-90%.
summary: Droperidol is an antidopaminergic medication used to prevent or treat nausea and as an antipsychotic. It is also used for rapid sedation in intensive-care settings and severe agitation.
